Implication: Performance estimates may be unstable and are not representative of the full MIMIC-IV population.
Only 18 events occurred in the primary 2-hour landmark cohort.
Sixteen of 18 positive cases had no selected physiological predictors available during the 0–2 hour observation window.
The number of future events declined substantially at later landmarks, increasing uncertainty.
Patient-separated cross-validation evaluates internal reproducibility but does not establish external clinical validity.
Multiple summaries of the same physiological variable are highly correlated, so individual feature importance should not be interpreted causally.
The 0.5 classification threshold was used analytically and should not be interpreted as an optimized clinical alert threshold.
